pathway.title: NABORS INDUSTRIES LTD — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The most important finding is concentration: Saudi Aramco accounted for about 30% of FY2025 consolidated operating revenues, the three largest contract drilling customers for about 41%, and about 41% of net receivables at September 30, 2026 were in Saudi Arabia. Because Aramco contracts are per rig and mainly run through SANAD, a customer decision to idle rigs cuts revenue and earnings without any contract termination, and the October release reports five suspended SANAD rigs against a quarter in which rig counts rose. That statement is management's, and until a filing confirms it the size of the effect cannot be stated.

The second finding is that leverage is moderate and has fallen on a gross basis only. Notes at face value fell from 2,529.1 to 2,050.0 US$m, gross leverage from 2.77x to 2.29x, but net debt moved only from 1,588.4 to 1,574.9 US$m, because the redemptions of the 2028 notes and part of the 2030 notes were paid from cash that fell from 940.7 to 475.1 US$m. Liquidity of cash plus the undrawn revolver therefore fell from 1,290.7 to 825.1 US$m. Third, the maturity profile is long: nothing matures before 250.0 US$m in June 2029, followed by 550.0, 550.0 and 700.0 US$m in 2030, 2031 and 2032, and the revolver runs to the earlier of June 17, 2029 and a springing date tied to the exchangeable notes; this limits refinancing risk for several years but concentrates 1,800.0 US$m in 2030 to 2032.

Fourth, free cash flow after net capital expenditures was 170.4 US$m on an LTM basis, 38.6 US$m for nine months 2026 and 74.5 US$m in Q3 2026, against annual coupons of 156.8 US$m on the notes outstanding; management guides full-year adjusted free cash flow of 100 to 110 US$m with SANAD newbuild spending included, and says Q3 spending was below forecast because milestones shifted. Fifth, SANAD is consolidated in full: 180.6 US$m of cash and 100% of its EBITDA are in the consolidated figures although Saudi Aramco owns half, redeemable noncontrolling interest of 502.7 US$m ranks as mezzanine equity, and Nabors has a disclosed backstop for its share of the first 25 rig purchases. Sixth, FY2025 earnings include Quail Tools, sold in August 2025, so LTM adjusted EBITDA of 893.6 US$m, against 912.7 US$m for FY2025, is the cleaner base; seventh, no sponsor, dividend recapitalisation or creditor-adverse action is documented, though related-party arrangements and the ownership gap remain to be monitored. Last, 2026 cash interest and the covenant EBITDA definition are not available, so coverage rests on interest expense (4.99x) and the reported covenant ratio.

runs.text: Strengths. Moderate leverage with a long runway: net leverage of 1.76x on face value, the first maturity in June 2029, and a revolver that is undrawn and matures no earlier than that date. Reported covenant headroom is wide, with interest coverage at 5.20x against 2.75x and minimum guarantor value at 99.8% against 90%, though the covenant definition is not available to test. Diversification across four segments and across the U.S. and international drilling, with technology and equipment segments that sell to third parties. A demonstrated willingness to repay debt in cash and to refinance ahead of maturity, shown by the 2025 refinancing and the 2026 redemptions. Adjusted EBITDA on an LTM basis is above 890 US$m with interest cover on interest expense of 4.99x and falling coupons.

Weaknesses. Concentration in Saudi Aramco and in SANAD, which supplies about 30% of revenue and carries a rig-purchase backstop, a call option on Nabors' interest on a change of control, and a redeemable noncontrolling interest. A smaller liquidity cushion of 825.1 US$m, of which 180.6 US$m is SANAD cash, and a receivables facility of 168.0 US$m sold whose term may end on April 1, 2027. Thin free cash flow cover of fixed charges and dependence on the timing of SANAD capital spending. Heavy dependence on issuer-defined adjusted EBITDA that excludes certain cash expenses and includes all of SANAD. Information gaps on guarantors, ranking, covenant definitions, backlog and ownership. History distorted by gains and disposals in FY2025.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Parker Drilling Company was acquired on March 11, 2025 as a wholly owned subsidiary for consideration of 4.8 million Nabors common shares plus a small cash payment, valued at about 180.6 US$m at the closing share price; the status is closed and the accounting is the acquisition method, with a bargain purchase gain recorded because the share price fell between signing on October 14, 2024 and closing (10-Q Q3 page:9; E11). No debt was raised for the purchase, but Parker's 13% second lien term loan of 177.8 US$m, which carried a change of control repayment trigger, was repaid on March 25, 2025 using the 2024 Credit Agreement (10-K page:105); revolver borrowings of 398.0 US$m in 2025 were fully repaid in 2025 (10-K page:83) and the revolver was undrawn at December 31, 2025, so the acquisition added no permanent secured debt on the filed evidence. Quail Tools, part of the Parker acquisition, was sold to Superior Energy Services, Inc. on August 20, 2025; the 10-K gives net consideration as 625.0 US$m including a working capital adjustment, and the 10-Q gives it as 600.0 US$m plus working capital adjustments, with cash of 375.0 US$m and a seller note of 250.0 US$m in both; the seller note was prepaid in full on October 9, 2025 (E12, E13). That difference is logged as a conflict below and is not reconciled.

On new debt, Nabors issued 700.0 US$m of 7.625% senior priority guaranteed notes due November 2032 on November 10, 2025 and used the net proceeds to redeem all of its 7.375% senior priority guaranteed notes due May 2027, of which 546.1 US$m remained, for about 557.1 US$m in cash including a 10.1 US$m premium (10-K page:104 and page:59). Earlier issues still outstanding are the 1.75% senior exchangeable notes of 250.0 US$m (February 2023), the 9.125% notes, 650.0 US$m outstanding at December 31, 2025 (indenture dated November 20, 2023), and the 8.875% notes of 550.0 US$m (indenture dated July 22, 2024) (10-K page:103 to page:104 and page:135). No new debt was issued in 2026 through the cutoff: the 7.50% senior guaranteed notes due January 2028 were redeemed on January 15, 2026, and 100.0 US$m of the 9.125% notes was redeemed for about 104.9 US$m in cash in the third quarter, taking notes at face value to 2,050.0 US$m (10-K page:103; 10-Q Q3 page:15; CP-1). On April 7, 2026 a joinder increased the credit agreement's letter of credit tranche by 25.0 US$m, and on September 4, 2025 the first amendment let Nabors Delaware repurchase up to 100.0 US$m of equity a year, reducing dividend capacity dollar for dollar (10-Q Q3 page:16). The special purpose acquisition company NETC II, co-sponsored with an entity owned by members of management and directors, failed to complete its planned combination with e2Companies; after litigation, a settlement on October 14, 2025 gave NETC II a secured promissory note from e2 of 29.23 US$m, and 10.6 US$m of settlement income was recorded in Other, net in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:30; 10-K page:113).

On August 26, 2026 Nabors issued about 0.4 million common shares for about 5.4 million Series B-1 preferred shares of Quaise Energy, Inc., a noncash exchange valued by reference to 35.0 US$m (10-Q Q3 page:17); this is an equity investment funded with shares, not cash or debt. As subsequent events after September 30, 2026 and before the cutoff, the October 27, 2026 release reports that SANAD deployed its 17th newbuild rig, that one more is scheduled for 2026 and two for the first quarter of 2027, that Nabors signed a multiyear contract to deploy one rig in Venezuela in early 2027, and that SANAD suspended five rigs (E14, E15, E16, E17). These are management statements in a furnished release; the filed 10-Q gives none of these counts. No sponsor, no dividend recapitalisation, no priming or uptier exchange and no debt-funded distribution appears in the pack. Nothing dated after the cutoff is used.

fields.value: Evidence: the debt note lists each series with its balance (September 2026 report page:15), the credit agreement has dated terms, a covenant ratio is reported each quarter end (E3, E19, E20, E17), and letter-of-credit facility availability is tabulated (E4). Risk mechanism: the maturity table by year exists only as of year-end 2025 (E15), before the January 2026 redemption of the 7.50% notes (10-K page:103) and the redemption of part of the 9.125% notes (E9; the October release places it in the third quarter), so a maturity wall copied from it would misstate refinancing timing. FY2025 consolidated adjusted EBITDA is not printed under that name in the annual report, which limits a like-for-like LTM build to the release period columns and the segment note, and the adjusted EBITDA definition is the issuer's own (E23). Consequence: CP-1 can run, must rebuild the maturity profile from the instrument list, must state the debt basis it uses (principal versus carrying value), and must label cash interest as FY2025 only. Verdict: READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS.

Risk mechanism: only filing descriptions exist for these transactions, with no executed merger or sale agreements, so deal terms and any creditor-relevant covenants of those documents cannot be checked; the release statement on rig suspensions (E21) is management language and the 10-Q only speaks of suspension notices in general (E11). Governance and ownership detail is limited to what the filings state; no sponsor exists in context. Consequence: CP-1A can run and must tag management statements as such. Verdict: READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS.

Consequence: CP-5 can run; it should treat the 10-Q as controlling over the release and flag basis differences instead of treating them as errors. Verdict: READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS.

fields.value: On the filed evidence, Nabors Industries Ltd entered 2026 with 2,529.1 US$m of notes at face value and ended Q3 2026 with 2,050.0, after redeeming the 7.50% notes due January 2028 and 100.0 US$m of the 9.125% notes due January 2030 with cash on hand. Because both redemptions were paid from cash, which fell from 940.7 to 475.1 US$m, net debt on a face-value basis moved only from 1,588.4 to 1,574.9 US$m, and net leverage on LTM adjusted EBITDA moved from 1.74x to 1.76x while gross leverage fell from 2.77x to 2.29x. Liquidity, cash plus the undrawn 350.0 US$m revolver, fell from 1,290.7 to 825.1 US$m, which remains sizeable against a first maturity in June 2029 but is a smaller cushion than at December 31, 2025. The reported covenant interest coverage ratio was 5.20x at September 30, 2026 against a minimum of 2.75x, and minimum guarantor value was 99.8% against 90%. Three features limit how far these figures can be pushed: consolidated cash, debt capacity and EBITDA include the 50%-owned SANAD venture; 2026 cash interest and the covenant EBITDA definition are not in the pack; and the FY2025 comparison includes Quail Tools. All figures below are issuer-reported or calculated from reported inputs, with the formula in Calculations.

fields.value: **Leverage.** Evidence: notes at face value fell from 2,529.1 to 2,050.0 US$m while LTM adjusted EBITDA is 893.6 US$m (Financials and credit metrics). Risk mechanism: the reduction was paid from cash, not from free cash flow, because operating cash flow less net capital expenditures was only 38.6 US$m in 9M 2026; net debt on face value is little changed, so the improvement in gross leverage does not add equal protection for creditors. Credit implication: gross leverage of 2.29x overstates the deleveraging; net leverage of 1.76x is the better reference and is flat to FY2025. Because FY2025 EBITDA includes at least 57.3 US$m from Quail Tools (Q2 2025 37.0 plus Q3 2025 20.3, calculated; Q1 2025 stub not supplied) which was sold in August 2025, the LTM figure is the cleaner earnings base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Coverage.** Evidence: interest expense fell from 215.4 to an LTM 179.2 US$m, and annual coupons on notes outstanding are 156.8 US$m against 194.3 US$m on the December 31, 2025 mix. Risk mechanism: coupons on the remaining notes are fixed, so interest expense should fall further toward the coupon run rate, while 2026 cash interest is not reported and the Q3 release says higher cash interest payments partly offset the sequential improvement in free cash flow (F15). Credit implication: cover on interest expense of 4.99x LTM is adequate and improving, and the reported covenant ratio of 5.20x is well above 2.75x, but the covenant definition cannot be tested from the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Cash flow quality.** Evidence: operating cash flow of 487.5 US$m in 9M 2026 against 448.8 US$m of net capital expenditures; working capital used 48.3 US$m (10-Q Q3 page:43); receivables rose to 511.7 US$m from 391.7 US$m, including related party receivables up to 211.5 US$m, a group that the 10-K says includes the joint venture partner Saudi Aramco (10-K page:114). Risk mechanism: growth in related party receivables and the Mexican late-payment history tie cash conversion to few counterparties, and the rise in receivables sold from 137.0 to 168.0 US$m, a calculated 31.0 US$m, supported operating cash flow in the nine months because sale proceeds are classified as operating (10-Q Q3 page:14). Credit implication: Q3 free cash flow of 74.5 US$m benefited from lower SANAD capital spending as milestones shifted to later periods (ER Q3 page:2 and page:3), so the full-year guidance of 100 to 110 US$m depends on Q4 delivery of 60 to 70 US$m.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Liquidity.** Evidence: cash and short-term investments of 475.1 US$m and an undrawn 350.0 US$m revolver give 825.1 US$m, down from 1,290.7 US$m. Risk mechanism: 180.6 US$m of the cash sits in SANAD, whose assets can be used to settle the venture's own obligations or be made available to its owners through dividends, distributions or an exchange of redeemable interests upon mutual agreement of the owners (10-Q Q3 page:13), and the receivables facility term may end on April 1, 2027 at the earliest. Credit implication: liquidity outside SANAD is lower than the headline; with no maturity before June 2029 and no borrowings, the near-term refinancing risk is low, but the cushion for a receivables facility non-renewal or an extended Saudi slowdown is thinner than at FY2025.

Credit implication: use LTM adjusted EBITDA as an issuer-defined base, not as a covenant-equivalent figure.

fields.value: On the filed evidence, Nabors Industries Ltd is an operating drilling contractor and not a sponsor-owned or recently recapitalised credit: no financial sponsor, controlling holder or dividend recapitalisation appears in the pack, and the transactions of the last two years are an equity-funded acquisition (Parker, closed March 11, 2025), a cash sale of the acquired Quail Tools business (August 20, 2025), a bond refinancing (November 10, 2025) and cash-funded note redemptions through Q3 2026. The business risk that matters most to a creditor is concentration: Saudi Aramco is both the largest customer, about 30% of FY2025 operating revenues, and the 50% partner in the consolidated SANAD joint venture, so revenue visibility, receivables, capital spending and a call option on Nabors' own interest all run through one relationship. The operating model is daywork contracting for rigs plus technology and equipment segments, with pricing set by dayrate and volume by rigs working; the filings do not quantify contract backlog or SANAD's own earnings, and the October release states a suspension of five SANAD rigs that the filed quarterly report does not. Governance behaviour is documented through related-party notes and the credit agreement's restricted payment terms rather than through any distribution or priming action; no behaviour in the Extraction-Oriented or Creditor-Adverse categories is evidenced, and ownership percentages cannot be stated because they sit in the proxy statement, which is not in the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Parker Drilling Company was acquired on March 11, 2025 as a wholly owned subsidiary for consideration of 4.8 million Nabors common shares plus a small cash payment, valued at about 180.6 US$m at the closing share price; the status is closed and the accounting is the acquisition method, with a bargain purchase gain recorded because the share price fell between signing on October 14, 2024 and closing (10-Q Q3 page:9; E11). No debt was raised for the purchase, but Parker's 13% second lien term loan of 177.8 US$m, which carried a change of control repayment trigger, was repaid on March 25, 2025 using the 2024 Credit Agreement (10-K page:105); revolver borrowings of 398.0 US$m in 2025 were fully repaid in 2025 (10-K page:83) and the revolver was undrawn at December 31, 2025, so the acquisition added no permanent secured debt on the filed evidence. Quail Tools, part of the Parker acquisition, was sold to Superior Energy Services, Inc. on August 20, 2025; the 10-K gives net consideration as 625.0 US$m including a working capital adjustment, and the 10-Q gives it as 600.0 US$m plus working capital adjustments, with cash of 375.0 US$m and a seller note of 250.0 US$m in both; the seller note was prepaid in full on October 9, 2025 (E12, E13). That difference is logged as a conflict below and is not reconciled.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On new debt, Nabors issued 700.0 US$m of 7.625% senior priority guaranteed notes due November 2032 on November 10, 2025 and used the net proceeds to redeem all of its 7.375% senior priority guaranteed notes due May 2027, of which 546.1 US$m remained, for about 557.1 US$m in cash including a 10.1 US$m premium (10-K page:104 and page:59). Earlier issues still outstanding are the 1.75% senior exchangeable notes of 250.0 US$m (February 2023), the 9.125% notes, 650.0 US$m outstanding at December 31, 2025 (indenture dated November 20, 2023), and the 8.875% notes of 550.0 US$m (indenture dated July 22, 2024) (10-K page:103 to page:104 and page:135). No new debt was issued in 2026 through the cutoff: the 7.50% senior guaranteed notes due January 2028 were redeemed on January 15, 2026, and 100.0 US$m of the 9.125% notes was redeemed for about 104.9 US$m in cash in the third quarter, taking notes at face value to 2,050.0 US$m (10-K page:103; 10-Q Q3 page:15; CP-1). On April 7, 2026 a joinder increased the credit agreement's letter of credit tranche by 25.0 US$m, and on September 4, 2025 the first amendment let Nabors Delaware repurchase up to 100.0 US$m of equity a year, reducing dividend capacity dollar for dollar (10-Q Q3 page:16). The special purpose acquisition company NETC II, co-sponsored with an entity owned by members of management and directors, failed to complete its planned combination with e2Companies; after litigation, a settlement on October 14, 2025 gave NETC II a secured promissory note from e2 of 29.23 US$m, and 10.6 US$m of settlement income was recorded in Other, net in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:30; 10-K page:113).

As subsequent events after September 30, 2026 and before the cutoff, the October 27, 2026 release reports that SANAD deployed its 17th newbuild rig, that one more is scheduled for 2026 and two for the first quarter of 2027, that Nabors signed a multiyear contract to deploy one rig in Venezuela in early 2027, and that SANAD suspended five rigs (E14, E15, E16, E17). These are management statements in a furnished release; the filed 10-Q gives none of these counts. No sponsor, no dividend recapitalisation, no priming or uptier exchange and no debt-funded distribution appears in the pack. Nothing dated after the cutoff is used.

fields.value: **Revenue durability and concentration.** Evidence: Saudi Aramco about 30% of FY2025 operating revenues, the three largest customers about 41%, contracts per rig through SANAD (E4, E5, E22), and 2026 suspension and reactivation notices in the Middle East (E24, E32). Risk mechanic: per-rig contracts let a customer idle rigs without a contract termination, so a suspension reduces revenue, EBITDA and receivable inflows at once while SANAD's newbuild obligations and Nabors' backstop continue; 41% of receivables sit in Saudi Arabia. Credit implication: debt service capacity depends on one counterparty's rig program, so the monitoring posture should track SANAD rig count and receivables from Saudi Arabia each quarter; the Q3 2026 filed rig counts rose, but management reports five suspended rigs after quarter end. Countering logged item: conflict C3 (Aramco share versus related-party revenue) means the size of the concentration is not fully pinned down.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Margin and cash-flow risk.** Evidence: daywork dayrate contracts, lower U.S. dayrates offset by volume, improving international pricing, and a management guide that includes a large SANAD newbuild program (E19, E23, E24, E27). Risk mechanic: margin depends on dayrate and rigs working, while SANAD capital spending is front-loaded and its timing has shifted to later periods. Credit implication: free cash flow after capital spending is sensitive to SANAD milestone timing, so the debt reduction already achieved came from cash balances rather than recurring surplus (CP-1).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Ownership and sponsor alignment.** Evidence: no sponsor or controlling holder is identified; change of control may accelerate debt and trigger a call option on the SANAD interest (E30). Risk mechanic: a control event would hit funding and the asset base together. Credit implication: sponsor alignment cannot be assessed beyond documented actions; behaviour is Supportive on deleveraging and Neutral on related-party items, and the ownership gap is a monitoring item.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Portfolio change.** Evidence: Parker acquired for shares and Quail Tools sold for cash within six months (E11, E12). Risk mechanic: FY2025 reported earnings include a business sold in August 2025 and a bargain purchase gain, so history overstates the continuing base. Credit implication: LTM figures from CP-1 are the cleaner base; the conflict on the sale price (C1) does not change the cash received of 375.0 US$m and the prepaid seller note of 250.0 US$m.

fields.value: The fundamental credit view of Nabors Industries Ltd as of 2026-11-05 is balanced, with financial risk moderate and business risk elevated, and the confidence is Medium because the evidence is complete enough to judge direction but several datapoints that would move the view are missing. On the financial side, notes at face value stand at 2,050.0 US$m, net debt is 1,574.9 US$m or 1.76x LTM adjusted EBITDA of 893.6 US$m, gross leverage is 2.29x, no note matures before the 250.0 US$m exchangeable notes in June 2029, the revolver is undrawn at 350.0 US$m, and the reported covenant interest coverage of 5.20x sits well above the 2.75x minimum. The weakening features are the use of cash to fund the deleveraging, which lowered liquidity from 1,290.7 to 825.1 US$m while net leverage stayed flat at 1.74x to 1.76x, and a free cash flow margin over fixed charges that is thin. On the business side, Saudi Aramco is about 30% of FY2025 operating revenues and the 50% partner in the consolidated SANAD venture, so revenue durability, receivables, a large newbuild capital program and a change-of-control call option all depend on one relationship; the filings show reactivations of Saudi rigs during 2026 and the October release reports five suspended SANAD rigs, which are management statements not yet in a filing. Governance evidence is neutral to supportive: debt has been repaid in cash, no sponsor or creditor-adverse action is documented, and the related-party arrangements are disclosed but only partly quantified. What would change the view: confirmed Saudi suspensions that cut earnings or collections, a non-renewal of the receivables facility, or evidence that SANAD cash and earnings are less accessible to creditors than the consolidated figures imply would weaken it; sustained free cash flow above fixed charges and further cash-funded debt reduction without eroding liquidity would strengthen it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The most important finding is concentration: Saudi Aramco accounted for about 30% of FY2025 consolidated operating revenues, the three largest contract drilling customers for about 41%, and about 41% of net receivables at September 30, 2026 were in Saudi Arabia. Because Aramco contracts are per rig and mainly run through SANAD, a customer decision to idle rigs cuts revenue and earnings without any contract termination, and the October release reports five suspended SANAD rigs against a quarter in which rig counts rose. That statement is management's, and until a filing confirms it the size of the effect cannot be stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second finding is that leverage is moderate and has fallen on a gross basis only. Notes at face value fell from 2,529.1 to 2,050.0 US$m, gross leverage from 2.77x to 2.29x, but net debt moved only from 1,588.4 to 1,574.9 US$m, because the redemptions of the 2028 notes and part of the 2030 notes were paid from cash that fell from 940.7 to 475.1 US$m. Liquidity of cash plus the undrawn revolver therefore fell from 1,290.7 to 825.1 US$m. Third, the maturity profile is long: nothing matures before 250.0 US$m in June 2029, followed by 550.0, 550.0 and 700.0 US$m in 2030, 2031 and 2032, and the revolver runs to the earlier of June 17, 2029 and a springing date tied to the exchangeable notes; this limits refinancing risk for several years but concentrates 1,800.0 US$m in 2030 to 2032.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, free cash flow after net capital expenditures was 170.4 US$m on an LTM basis, 38.6 US$m for nine months 2026 and 74.5 US$m in Q3 2026, against annual coupons of 156.8 US$m on the notes outstanding; management guides full-year adjusted free cash flow of 100 to 110 US$m with SANAD newbuild spending included, and says Q3 spending was below forecast because milestones shifted. Fifth, SANAD is consolidated in full: 180.6 US$m of cash and 100% of its EBITDA are in the consolidated figures although Saudi Aramco owns half, redeemable noncontrolling interest of 502.7 US$m ranks as mezzanine equity, and Nabors has a disclosed backstop for its share of the first 25 rig purchases. Sixth, FY2025 earnings include Quail Tools, sold in August 2025, so LTM adjusted EBITDA of 893.6 US$m, against 912.7 US$m for FY2025, is the cleaner base; seventh, no sponsor, dividend recapitalisation or creditor-adverse action is documented, though related-party arrangements and the ownership gap remain to be monitored. Last, 2026 cash interest and the covenant EBITDA definition are not available, so coverage rests on interest expense (4.99x) and the reported covenant ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Moderate leverage with a long runway: net leverage of 1.76x on face value, the first maturity in June 2029, and a revolver that is undrawn and matures no earlier than that date. Reported covenant headroom is wide, with interest coverage at 5.20x against 2.75x and minimum guarantor value at 99.8% against 90%, though the covenant definition is not available to test. Diversification across four segments and across the U.S. and international drilling, with technology and equipment segments that sell to third parties. A demonstrated willingness to repay debt in cash and to refinance ahead of maturity, shown by the 2025 refinancing and the 2026 redemptions. Adjusted EBITDA on an LTM basis is above 890 US$m with interest cover on interest expense of 4.99x and falling coupons.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Concentration in Saudi Aramco and in SANAD, which supplies about 30% of revenue and carries a rig-purchase backstop, a call option on Nabors' interest on a change of control, and a redeemable noncontrolling interest. A smaller liquidity cushion of 825.1 US$m, of which 180.6 US$m is SANAD cash, and a receivables facility of 168.0 US$m sold whose term may end on April 1, 2027. Thin free cash flow cover of fixed charges and dependence on the timing of SANAD capital spending. Heavy dependence on issuer-defined adjusted EBITDA that excludes certain cash expenses and includes all of SANAD. Information gaps on guarantors, ranking, covenant definitions, backlog and ownership. History distorted by gains and disposals in FY2025.
